bandReport.notes:
Q60-Q100, 41 questions, contiguous with no gaps. Printed page = index + 1 throughout, footer A - KPRS-T-MTE on every page, confirming the config pre-pass.

SEAM WITH b1 IS CLEAN. Opened p22 (b1's last page, printed 23) without transcribing it: it carries Q55-Q59 and Q59 completes on it, options and all. No Directions block is open at the boundary, so b1 owns nothing that runs into my band and I own nothing that starts in theirs. My first question Q60 opens at the top of p24's left column.

Q100 COMPLETES ON p42 (printed 43) WITH ALL FOUR OPTIONS - the config comment flagged this as unconfirmed and it is now VERIFIED, two ways. (1) Q100's stem and its four options are wholly on p42's right column. (2) I rendered the un-rendered tail of the booklet direct from the PDF: indices 43-46 are SPACE FOR ROUGH WORK (alternating Hindi/English, printed 44-47) and index 47 is the English cover, exactly as config predicted. The cover independently corroborates the paper's shape - 'This Test Booklet contains 100 items (questions)', Series A, T.B.C. KPRS-T-MTE, Time Allowed Two Hours, Maximum Marks 100, one-third penalty. The booklet is 48 pages and has no text layer on any of them.

SETS. TEN Directions blocks fall in this band and every one of them STARTS inside it, so I own all twenty members and none straddles a band boundary: D81-82 (starts p36, member Q82 read forward onto p38), D83-84, D85-86, D87-88 (all p38), D89-90, D91-92, D93-94 (all p40), D95-96, D97-98, D99-100 (all p42). Each pair is contiguous in number and both members carry identical verbatim context. Note the last Directions block of the paper opens on p42 and closes on p42.

DATA SUFFICIENCY BLOCK, Q71-Q80. Ten consecutive items share the preamble 'A Question is given followed by two Statements I and II...' but the preamble is REPRINTED IN FULL above each one, so they are ten standalone questions, not a Directions set - no setLabel, preamble kept in the stem.

OPTION (d) IS NOT CONSTANT ACROSS THOSE TEN AND THIS IS THE EASIEST WAY TO CORRUPT THIS PAGE RANGE. Options (a)(b)(c) are word-for-word identical in all ten. Option (d) is 'The Question cannot be answered even by using both the Statements together' on Q71, Q72, Q75, Q76, Q77 - and 'The Question can be answered even without using both the Statements' on Q73, Q74, Q78, Q79, Q80. Each was read off its own page rather than copied from a neighbour.

DECIMALS: the booklet sets a raised middle dot (0.5, 5.24, 7.5, 5.12) and these are transcribed as full stops per the brief.

CURRENCY: the D89-90 stimulus prints the rupee SYMBOL with no space (16,000 / 24,000 / 4800). Transcribed as 'Rs. 16,000' etc., following the corpus convention - the 19 sibling papers use 'Rs.' and the rupee symbol appears in zero committed band files. Digit grouping is preserved as printed, which is why 4800 carries no comma while 16,000 and 24,000 do.

NO FIGURES IN THIS BAND, and that was measured rather than assumed. Scanning all 41 stems and contexts for figure/diagram/given below/shown below/adjoining/graph returns exactly two hits, Q64 and Q65, and both are the boilerplate 'Select the answer using the code given below' / 'Which of the statements given below is/are correct' - neither points at a printed diagram. The geometry items (Q63 tangent, Q64 cyclic quadrilateral, Q65 parallel chords, Q67 intersecting right triangles, Q74 midpoint quadrilateral) all state their configuration fully in words, and p24-p42 carry no printed artwork at all. So hasFigure is set on nothing. Worth knowing, because figures usually cluster in a booklet's closing pages and this one has none.

NOTHING WAS ILLEGIBLE. Every sign, exponent and fraction that could change a claim was cropped from the source PNG at 5-8x and read again rather than inferred: the (0.5)^-n exponent on Q78, the negative options on Q81/Q82/Q91/Q94, the p^4q^2 + p^2q^4 exponents on Q94, both surd stimuli, and every option fraction on Q83/Q84/Q95/Q96/Q98/Q100.

ONE INVENTED SUBTOPIC, flagged on the question: Q76 'Inequalities Involving Powers'. The Inequalities chapter lists only Linear, Absolute Value and Quadratic, and Q76 asks whether r^n < 1 given bounds on r^2 and r^3. Recorded as a finding for the catalog extension pass rather than forced into a bad fit.

NO MISPRINTS FOUND. Two cosmetic notes, neither flagged because neither changes a claim: Q77 prints 'Is (p^2 + q^2) always composite number' with no article, transcribed as printed; and Q74 prints 'mid-points', where the hyphen falls at a line break so hyphenation and the genuine spelling are indistinguishable - kept as 'mid-points', the usual UPSC form. Q69's 'dimen-sions' IS a line-break hyphenation and was joined.

questions.stem: The minute hand of a clock is 15 cm long and sweeps an area of \(15\pi\) \(\text{cm}^2\) on the dial of the clock. How much angle does it describe during this period ?
The diameter of a copper solid sphere is 6 cm. The sphere is melted and recast into a wire. If the diameter of the wire is 0.5 cm, then what is the length of the wire ?
A square and a rectangle have the same perimeter p and their areas differ by q units. What is the square of the difference between the length and breadth of the rectangle ?
questions.subtopic: Comparison of Areas for Equal Perimeter

questions.stem: A triangle PQR is inscribed in a circle with its centre at O. A tangent PT is drawn at P such that \(\angle QPT = 36^\circ\). What is \(\angle POQ\) equal to ?

ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral. AB and DC are produced to meet at P. Which of the following statements is/are correct ?

I. \(\triangle PAD\) is similar to \(\triangle PBC\)

II. \(\angle PAD + \angle PDA = \angle PBC + \angle PCB\)

Select the answer using the code given below :

Let O be the centre of a circle. Let the chords AB = 10 cm and CD = 24 cm be two parallel chords of the circle. The two chords are on opposite side of the centre and the distance between them is 17 cm. Let P be the midpoint of AB and Q be the midpoint of CD. Further, the points O and A, the points O and C, the points A and C are joined. Which of the statements given below is/are correct ?

I. Area of triangle OAP is equal to area of triangle OCQ.

II. Area of triangle OAC is equal to \(102\) \(\text{cm}^2\).

Select the answer using the code given below :

A metallic sheet of rectangular shape is 48 cm \(\times\) 36 cm. From each corner a square of side x cm is cut off and an open box is made of the remaining sheet. If the box holds 5.12 litre of water, then what is the value of x ?
Two triangles ABC right-angled at A and DBC right-angled at D are drawn such that AC and DB intersect at P. If AP = x, PC = y and BP = z, then what is (AC + BD) equal to ?
In a triangle ABC, AB = 18 cm, BC = 22 cm and AC = 15 cm. The bisector of \(\angle BAC\) intersects BC at D. What is (BD \(\times\) DC) equal to ?

The volume of a cube is \(8\) \(\text{cm}^3\) and is equal to the volume of a cuboid of length x, breadth y and height z, where x, y and z are natural numbers \((x > y > z)\). Let n be the number of such cuboids with different dimensions. What is the value of n ?

Let x, y, z (all prime) be the length, breadth and height respectively of a cuboid with \(x > y > z\). The volume of the cuboid is \(30k^3\) cubic units, where k is a natural number. What is the total surface area of the cuboid ?
